metadata.displayText:
Progressão Temporal e Ciclos de Jogo

• Envelhecimento anual linear: Avanço da vida do personagem em blocos fechados de exatamente um ano por clique através de um botão central.
• Progressão por frações de ano: Avanço temporal fragmentado de forma mensal ou trimestral para maior controle das ações cotidianas.
• Passagem de turno baseada em ações: O tempo flui estritamente de acordo com o gasto de pontos de ação e movimentação do personagem pelo mapa.
• Ciclo Dia/Noite por passos: Avanço horário dinâmico onde explorações e viagens consomem frações do relógio global, alterando taxas de emboscada.
• Desafios semanais sincronizados: Eventos ao vivo via nuvem com metas ultra-especificas que premiam o jogador com acessórios cosméticos permanentes.

📊 Atributos e Sistemas Biológicos Ocultos

• Atributos biológicos básicos: Barras estáticas de status visíveis que medem Felicidade, Saúde, Inteligência e Aparência.
• Gestão de atributos psicológicos: Barras dedicadas para o controle de Energia, Saúde Mental, Fadiga e níveis de Stress.
• Sistema de Karma oculto: Modificador invisível de sorte que aumenta com boas ações e reduz drasticamente a chance de acidentes e falhas trágicas.
• Mecânica de Loucura oculta: Atributo que dita a propensão do personagem e de NPCs a aceitarem desafios insanos ou iniciarem agressões físicas.
• Fórmula de fertilidade biológica: Atributo fixado no nascimento que sofre declínio progressivo com a idade e dita o sucesso de gravidezes e fertilizações.
• Vetor de envelhecimento segmentado: Cálculo de perda estética individualizada que simula calvície, rugas e ganho de gordura localizada.
• Mecânica de Força de Combate: Atributo oculto inflacionado por treinos que define o sucesso em brigas de rua, assaltos e autodefesa.
• Desgaste biológico e fome: Sistema de necessidades físicas que exige consumo de rações e água para evitar a perda permanente de Vida Máxima (HP).

Saúde, Dependências e Condições Médicas

• Mecânica de Vício (Addiction): Gatilho ativado por RNG após o consumo de substâncias ou apostas, exigindo internações em clínicas de reabilitação.
• Doenças mentais psicossomáticas: Diagnósticos de Depressão, Ansiedade e TOC que aplicam debuffs severos em estudos e alteram opções textuais.
• Identidade e transição de gênero: Mecânica de descoberta de sexualidade na puberdade, permitindo cirurgias de redesignação e alteração de nome.
• Procedimentos estéticos invasivos: Menu de cirurgias plásticas com taxas ocultas de erro médico que deformam a aparência do avatar de forma permanente.
• Infecções de ferimentos por turno: Sistema onde feridas abertas em combate inflamam se não tratadas, drenando a vida do personagem a cada passo.
• Aposentadoria de ofício por invalidez: Mecânica onde o envelhecimento dobra o custo de fadiga para trabalhos braçais, forçando a migração de carreira.

👪 Relacionamentos, Hereditariedade e Sociedade

• Hereditariedade e linhagem dinástica: Mecânica de transferência de consciência, posses e capital acumulado para um herdeiro após a morte.
• Geração procedural de relacionamentos: Conexão com pais, cônjuges e filhos medidos por barras de afinidade e modificados por presentes ou conversas.
• Interações sociais categorizadas por tom: Sistema de diálogo que permite escolher abordagens específicas (flertar, insultar, conversar, apoiar).
• Mecânica de herança fracionada: Testamento avançado que permite a divisão exata de porcentagens patrimoniais entre múltiplos herdeiros.
• Casamento com separação de bens: Acordos pré-nupciais que protegem o patrimônio líquido contra divórcios causados por traições ou brigas.
• Ordens de restrição e stalking: Sistema de perseguição de ex-parceiros movidos por alta loucura e rancor pós-término.
• Criação de NPCs customizados: Injeção de nomes e perfis personalizados do mundo real no banco de dados procedural do simulador.

Carreiras, Negócios e Educação

• Profissões premium com minijogos: Carreiras especiais estruturadas (Ator, Músico, Atleta, Político) com loops de jogabilidade dedicados.
• Equação de performance corporativa: Sistema de promoção profissional calibrado pelo equilíbrio diário entre energia, inteligência e estresse.
• Gestão de franquias corporativas: Abertura de empresas com controle de fornecedores, controle de qualidade e cadeia de suprimentos.
• Criação de produtos e pesquisa de mercado: Lançamento de mercadorias definindo margem de lucro, marketing e previsão de demanda industrial.
• Relações trabalhistas e recursos humanos: Mecânica de contratação, concessão de bônus e demissão de funcionários para conter greves e processos.
• Árvores de especialização técnica: Progressão de cargos baseada em qualificações acadêmicas e entrevistas de emprego textuais.
• Clínica de popularidade escolar: Divisão de estudantes em camarilhas e clubes que moldam os atributos e o ganho de status na adolescência.
• Atividades extracurriculares competitivas: Ingressar em times de esporte ou debate escolar através de minijogos de rendimento.

Mercado de Capitais, Bens e Imobiliário

• Mercado de ações e criptomoedas dinâmico: Flutuações anuais com ciclos de bolha financeira gerados de forma puramente procedural.
• Manutenção e custos de propriedade: Cobrança de impostos prediais, taxas de seguro e reformas anuais para veículos e imóveis.
• Mercado imobiliário de locação (Landlord): Atuação direta como senhorio, gerenciando histórico de crédito de inquilinos e ordens de despejo.
• Investimento-anjo em startups: Injeção de capital em rodadas de financiamento privado com riscos de diluição de ações ou falência.
• Imposto sobre grandes fortunas dinástico: Confisco de até 40% do patrimônio líquido em dinheiro pelo estado na transição de herança em países específicos.
• Gacha diário de relíquias (Heirlooms): Spawn de itens raros a cada 24 horas reais com valorização e depreciação financeira no mercado de antiguidades.
• Museu particular de exibições: Galeria de exposição de bens exóticos e raridades com cobrança de ingressos para monetizar a fama.
• Mineração de ativos digitais: Montagem de rigs de mineração de criptoativos com custos reais de eletricidade e desgaste de hardware.

Ilegalidade, Crimes e Vida Prisional

• Mecânica de crimes e roubos: Sistema de furtos de veículos, assaltos a residências e piquetes baseados em RNG e níveis de inteligência.
• Mini-games de infiltração e labirinto: Desafios em grade e turnos para escapar de prisões ou invadir propriedades sem ser detectado.
• Sistemas de assassinatos e fatalidade: Métodos de execução que cruzam discrição e letalidade contra o risco de captura policial instantânea.
• Iniciação e hierarquia mafiosa: Execução de extorsões para provar lealdade a sindicatos do crime, evoluindo de associado até chefe supremo.
• Mecânica de informante (Rato do FBI): Coleta de evidências textuais contra a própria organização criminosa em troca de imunidade e proteção.
• Ecossistema das grades carcerárias: Menu de sobrevivência prisional englobando participação em gangues internas, rebeliões e trabalho forçado.
• Mercado paralelo e contrabandistas: Compra de itens falsificados ou ilegais em camelôs com riscos de golpes, apreensões ou confisco.

Fama, Redes Sociais e Influência

• Engajamento digital procedural: Criação de postagens em plataformas que emulam redes reais, lidando com algoritmos, viralização e cancelamentos.
• Monetização de celebridade: Ativação de abas de publicidade, comerciais de TV, ensaios fotográficos e escrita de autobiografias para inflacionar ganhos.
• Mecânica de monarquia e respeito real: Geração de linhagens nobres onde o prestígio público substitui a fama e garante poderes executivos absolutos.
• Criação de seitas e cultos: Recrutamento de seguidores, definição de doutrinas isoladas e cobrança de dízimos para enriquecimento messiânico.
• Simulação aeroespacial astronáutica: Treinamento de gravidade, calibração de dados de telemetria e exploração de anomalias espaciais em missões.

🗺️ Macroeconomia, Logística e Sobrevivência (Mundo Aberto)

• Ecossistema socioeconômico autônomo: NPCs operam suas próprias vidas, casando, trabalhando e morrendo de forma independente do jogador.
• Algoritmo de oferta e demanda regional: Cidades com produções de commodities específicas onde a escassez ou superprodução altera os preços de compra e venda.
• Simulação de rotas e arbitragem: Exploração de brechas de mercado causadas por climas e guerras para comprar insumos baratos e vender caro em outras províncias.
• Desgaste de equipamentos e durabilidade: Armas e ferramentas perdem eficácia com o uso, exigindo manutenção paga em oficinas e ferreiros.
• Mecânica de sobrecarga por peso (Encumbrance): O peso total do inventário confronta a força do herói, reduzindo a velocidade de viagem e aumentando o consumo de rações.
• Alfândega e pedágios territoriais: Fiscalização de guardas em portões de cidades com base em atributos de subterfúgio para barrar itens proibidos.
• Contratação de caravanas automatizadas: Criação de linhas comerciais secundárias com contratação de mulas e guardas para gerar lucro passivo pelo mapa.
• Quadro de contratos e reputação de facções: Missões em tavernas que aumentam o prestígio com uma guilda enquanto reduzem a influência com organizações rivais.
• Agiotagem coerciva de taverna: Empréstimos rápidos sem colateral, mas com juros abusivos que disparam inimigos físicos no mapa em caso de inadimplência.
• Mecânica de acampamento em estradas: Criação de zonas de descanso temporárias para recuperar vida, necessitando de fogueiras para repelir animais selvagens.

⚔️ Combate Textual e Regras de Interface

• Rolagem de iniciativa oculta: Confronto mecânico de agilidade para ditar quem executa a primeira ação em encontros hostis.
• Zonas de dano e blindagem corporal: Divisão de acertos em membros específicos (Cabeça, Tórax, Pernas), calculando a defesa com base nos equipamentos vestidos.
• Efeitos de status hostis em combate: Aplicação de debuffs textuais como sangramento, atordoamento, cegueira e envenenamento durante os turnos.
• Árvore de meta-progresso por conquistas: Desafios de sistema que, quando completados, desbloqueiam cenários iniciais, profissões ou itens estéticos permanentemente.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand VIVA into a polished Portuguese, offline, single-player life-simulation SPA with interconnected lifestyle, health, identity, social, property, collection, and future-progression systems.
- Implement the temporal progression and biological attributes foundation first.

## Requirements
- Preserve `SAVE_KEY = 'viva-save-v2'`, `localStorage`, centralized `state`, `render()`, `commit()`, `runAction()`, and `addEvent()` architecture.
- Preserve existing mechanics, dead-life guards, cooldown rollback, event ordering, save validation, sanitization, responsive UI, Portuguese labels, and visible feedback.
- Keep annual one-year progression through `#ageBtn`, while allowing future monthly, quarterly, or action-based time modes.
- Add visible biological and psychological attributes plus hidden karma, madness, fertility, and combat systems incrementally.
- Keep changes uncommitted unless explicitly requested.
- Browser visual verification remains optional because Chromium is unavailable.

## Decisions
- Extend the existing architecture incrementally instead of replacing it.
- Use normalized persistent state with defaults in `initialState()` and validation/sanitization in `loadState()`.
- Keep annual progression as the active mode while storing temporal metadata for future extensions.
- Integrate biological wear, needs, fatigue, mental health, maximum HP, fertility, and combat effects into `advanceYear()`.
- Reuse existing renderers, modal flows, dashboard controls, and Portuguese UI patterns.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added normalized `temporal` state with `mode`, `lastAdvance`, and `totalMonths`.
- Added normalized `attributes` state covering intelligence, appearance, energy, mental health, fatigue, madness, fertility, aging, hunger, hydration, maximum HP, and combat strength.
- Added legacy-save validation and clamping for temporal and biological attributes.
- Updated annual progression to increment temporal metadata and apply aging, fatigue, hunger, hydration, mental-health, madness, fertility, max-HP, combat-strength, energy, and biological-wear effects.
- Updated combat display to use calculated `attributes.combatStrength`.
- Added `renderAttributes()` and wired it into `render()`.
- Added Portuguese dashboard panel for temporal status and visible biological attributes.
- Added responsive styling for the attributes panel in `style.css`.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Existing systems remain intact, including lifestyle, collections, exotic pets, landlord, addiction, mental health, identity, prison, finances, social media, and annual events.

### Active
- Review the complete diff and verify that the new temporal/attribute UI and state integration do not conflict with existing markup or styles.
- Improve attribute semantics and feedback where needed, especially hidden `madness`, `karma`, and combat interactions.
- Consider adding more explicit visible status for age-related wear and temporal progression.

### Blocked
- Browser visual verification is unavailable because Chromium is not installed at `/home/runner/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1243/chrome-linux64/chrome`.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the complete uncommitted diff, including the unexpected existing `README.md` changes, before modifying further.
2. Run targeted static checks and inspect `index.html`, `app.js`, and `style.css` around the new attributes panel.
3. Fix any integration, styling, or persistence issues found.
4. Add tests or lightweight runtime checks for legacy saves and annual progression if practical.
5. Leave all changes uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: central state, save validation, rendering, annual progression, actions, and event logic.
- `index.html`: dashboard markup, annual progression control, and new temporal/attribute panel.
- `style.css`: responsive styling for the new attributes panel and existing dashboard systems.
- `README.md`: contains existing uncommitted documentation changes that must be reviewed before finalizing.
- `capture.sh`: optional browser visual-validation utility.
- `start.sh`: local application wrapper.
- `startup.sh`: auxiliary startup wrapper.

## Important Context
- Save key is exactly `viva-save-v2`.
- Annual progression is implemented in `advanceYear()` and triggered by `#ageBtn`.
- New state fields are `state.temporal` and `state.attributes`; legacy saves are merged from `initialState()` and sanitized in `loadState()`.
- `renderAttributes()` targets `#temporalStatus`, `#agingNote`, `#intelligenceScore`, `#appearanceScore`, `#mentalHealthScore`, `#fertilityScore`, `#hydrationScore`, `#hungerScore`, `#fatigueScore`, and `#maxHpScore`.
- `state.health` is capped by `attributes.maxHp` during annual progression.
- Changes remain uncommitted.

⚖️ Mecânicas Jurídicas, Processuais e Direito de Família

• Pensão alimentícia e custódia (Alimony): No divórcio, se o cônjuge tiver renda menor, o jogo deduz um valor fixo do seu salário por turno. A custódia dos filhos dita quem gerencia a barra de afinidade deles.
• Apelação e extradição criminal: Opção de contratar bancas de advogados para recorrer de sentenças de prisão ou contestar mandados de extradição ao fugir para outro país.
• Execução de testamento com dívidas: Se o personagem morre falido, as dívidas de hipoteca e empréstimos são deduzidas do saldo do herdeiro, podendo fazê-lo iniciar a nova vida no negativo.

🐕 Genética de Pets e Criação (Breeding)

• Cruzamento procedural de animais: Seleção de matrizes e reprodutores baseada em pedigree, gerando filhotes com atributos de pureza e mutações estéticas para venda.
• Treinamento de comportamento animal: Comandos textuais para corrigir níveis de agressividade de pets, reduzindo a chance de eles atacarem visitas ou o próprio dono.

🏢 Micro-Sistemas de Emprego e Sindicato

• Mecânica de greve e piquete: Opção de paralisar o trabalho para exigir aumentos salariais, lidando com o risco de demissão por justa causa ou repressão.
• Testes de drogas corporativos: Exames surpresa que cruzam o seu histórico oculto de consumo de substâncias; falhar resulta em demissão imediata e quebra de reputação.

🎒 Sobrevivência Urbana e Sem-Teto (AltLife/Living World)

• Mecânica de vadiagem e mendicância: Se o saldo zerar e você perder os imóveis, o menu muda para sobrevivência de rua, permitindo pedir esmolas ou revirar lixeiras por itens.
• Invasão de propriedades abandonadas (Squatting): Ocupar imóveis vazios para fugir do frio e recuperar energia, com risco de despejo policial a cada turno.

🔮 Sistemas Místicos e Ocultismo Legados

• Consultas com médiuns e exorcistas: Mecânica para lidar com propriedades assombradas (fantasmas reduzem a felicidade do imóvel e travam a venda), exigindo rituais com taxas de sucesso baseadas em Karma.
• Bruxaria e curandeirismo: Uso de medicinas alternativas em vilarejos (Living World) para curar doenças que a medicina tradicional falhou, com risco de envenenamento.

## Integration report

No files were modified. Relevant files:

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js`
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css`

### 1. Legal and family systems

#### Existing legal-adjacent state and behavior

`app.js` already contains criminal and incarceration state:

- `state.prison`: gang, protection, respect, work, study, riot risk — `app.js:30`
- `state.arrestCount`, `state.prisonYears`, `state.deathCause` — `app.js:37`
- Prison normalization and validation — `app.js:87-88`
- `renderPrison()` updates `#prisonDetails` — `app.js:207-210`
- `prisonAction(type)` supports protection, prison work, study, and riot choices — `app.js:446-453`
- Criminal activity can increase arrest count and prison time — `app.js:662`
- `#prisonStatus` is rendered in the Patrimônio statistics area — `app.js:348`; markup is in `index.html:36`

Landlord eviction is the only explicit court-related system:

- `landlordAction('evict')` starts a two-year legal eviction process — `app.js:480`
- Annual processing completes evictions and removes tenants — `app.js:508-515`
- The rental UI displays a judicial-process notice in `#landlordList` — `app.js:228-243`

There is no dedicated legal state object, case-management system, lawyer/court UI, legal actions, or legal-specific CSS.

#### Existing family system

State:

- `partnerId`
- `children`
- `generations`
- Relationships and romance data — `app.js:38, 42-46`

Markup:

- `#relacoesView`
- `#meetBtn`
- `#childrenList`
- `#childBtn`
- `#adoptBtn`
- `#generationsList` — `index.html:35`

Event wiring:

- `#meetBtn` calls `activity('dating')` — `app.js:693`
- Dating creates a romance relationship through the `dating` activity — `app.js:660`
- `#childBtn` opens a confirmation modal, then runs `family-child` — `app.js:694`
- `#adoptBtn` opens a confirmation modal, then runs `family-adopt` — `app.js:695`

Family actions already enforce:

- Minimum age
- Partner requirement for biological child planning
- Fertility threshold
- Money and energy costs
- Adoption age and resource requirements

Recommended legal/family insertion point: add a legal panel beside the existing family panels in `#relacoesView`, or create a dedicated section using the same `.career-grid` and `.panel` structure. Use `openModal()` / `openChoiceModal()` for custody, marriage, divorce, adoption review, guardianship, or legal disputes.

---

### 2. Pets

#### Existing state and normalization

`app.js` initializes:

```js
exoticPets: { pets: [], accidents: 0 }
```

at `app.js:34`.

Save/load normalization:

- Pets must be objects
- Maximum of 12 pets
- Accident count is clamped to nonnegative values — `app.js:108-109`

#### Existing actions and rendering

`buyExoticPet(type)` supports:

- `tigre`
- `cobra`

It enforces adulthood and sufficient funds, adds the pet, increases stress, and records an event — `app.js:479`.

Rendering occurs in `renderLifestyle()`:

- Target: `#petsList`
- Displays pet name, type, icon, and annual maintenance — `app.js:221-227`

Annual effects:

- Pet maintenance is included in expenses — `app.js:501-503`
- Pet accidents can reduce health and money — `app.js:516-520`
- Accident count is incremented and an event is created

Event wiring:

```js
$$('[data-buy-pet]').forEach(button =>
  button.onclick = () => {
    buyExoticPet(button.dataset.buyPet);
    render();
  }
);
```

— `app.js:689`.

The corresponding pet markup is in the lifestyle/system area of `index.html:32`, although the line is highly compressed.

Risks:

- Pet records are only lightly normalized; individual fields such as `name`, `type`, and `cost` are not strongly validated.
- The purchase action does not appear to check the 12-pet cap before pushing a new pet. The cap is enforced during load normalization, not necessarily during live play.
- There is no pet removal, care, licensing, veterinary, or naming interaction beyond the generated name.

---

### 3. Employment and career

#### Existing state

`career` is initialized with:

- Title: Product Designer
- Company: Estúdio Aurora
- Salary: R$7,800
- Level: 4
- Skill: 78
- Employed: true
- Satisfaction: 74
- Remote: false

— `app.js:39`.

Career data is included in save/load object validation — `app.js:67-69`.

#### Existing markup

The career section is:

- `#carreiraView`
- Career page heading and controls
- Existing career panel/cards — `index.html:34`

The primary dashboard employment interaction is `#jobBtn`; the button is wired to `careerMenu()` — `app.js:692`.

#### Existing actions

`careerMenu()` opens a choice modal with:

- Salary negotiation
- Skill development
- Remote work toggle
- Resignation or re-employment

— `app.js:666-675`.

Career changes affect:

- Salary
- Satisfaction
- Stress
- Skill
- Employment status
- Company and title
- Annual income

Annual income is processed in `advanceYear()` and is suppressed while the character is imprisoned — `app.js:497-503`.

Career rendering updates:

- `.career-hero`
- `.career-salary`
- `#skills`

The exact render function is part of the central render flow around `app.js:268`.

Education is also linked to employment. Completing courses such as Direito, Medicina, MBA, or Artes changes the opportunity selected when the player returns to work — `app.js:673`.

Recommended employment insertion points:

- Add employment-specific choices inside `careerMenu()`.
- Add UI to `#carreiraView` using existing career panels.
- Reuse the modal system for interviews, layoffs, promotions, workplace conflicts, and benefits.
- Add any new career fields to both `initialState()` and load normalization.

Risks:

- Career rendering assumes expected career fields exist.
- New employment state must be normalized defensively because saved state is merged from `localStorage`.
- Prison status currently blocks annual income but does not appear to preserve a detailed employment history.

---

### 4. Homelessness and housing

There is no dedicated homelessness system or `homelessness` state field.

#### Existing housing-adjacent systems

The code does contain:

- Property finances — `finances.property`
- Home goal — `goals.home`
- Landlord state:
  - `properties`
  - `tenants`
  - `evictionLock`

— `app.js:35, 38, 40`.

`landlordAction(type)` supports:

- Buying a rental property
- Finding a tenant
- Collecting rent
- Starting an eviction process

— `app.js:480`.

Annual housing behavior includes:

- Rental income
- Tenant arrears
- Tenant credit changes
- Property damage
- Eviction completion
- Judicial lock duration

— `app.js:502, 508-515`.

Markup:

- `#patrimonioView`
- Property and vehicle values
- `#landlordList`
- `#propertyValue`
- `#homeGoal`
- `#prisonStatus`
- Generic “Gerenciar” button

— `index.html:36`.

Event wiring:

```js
$$('[data-landlord]').forEach(button =>
  button.onclick = () => {
    landlordAction(button.dataset.landlord);
    render();
  }
);
```

— `app.js:690`.

The Patrimônio “Gerenciar” button opens an investment/travel modal, not a housing-specific menu — `app.js:703`.

#### Integration recommendation

A homelessness system could be added as:

```js
housing: {
  status: 'housed',
  shelter: null,
  rent: 0,
  monthsHomeless: 0,
  evictionRisk: 0
}
```

The best UI location is `#patrimonioView`, next to the existing property panel, or a new housing system panel inside the dashboard.

Potential states/actions:

- Stable housing
- Renting
- Couch surfing
- Shelter
- Street homelessness
- Applying for assistance
- Finding work or temporary housing
- Eviction appeal
- Rehousing

Important risk: homelessness should be modeled separately from `landlord`, because landlord ownership currently represents the player as a property owner rather than a tenant or unhoused character.

---

### 5. Occult system

No dedicated occult state, action, markup, event binding, or CSS was found.

The only occult-adjacent element is the character-creation trait:

```html
<option>espiritual</option>
```

in `index.html:40`.

The trait also influences annual stress:

```js
state.stress = clamp(
  state.stress + 3 + (deficit ? 5 : 0)
  - (state.trait === 'espiritual' ? 2 : 0)
);
```

— `app.js:529`.

There are also general spiritual/reflective actions such as meditation, but these are not an occult system:

- `activity('meditate')` — `app.js:661`
- Purpose and mental-health UI
- Generic `spiritual` personality trait

Recommended insertion point:

- Add an occult system panel to the dashboard’s existing `.systems-grid`.
- Add state such as `occult`, `rituals`, `belief`, `omens`, or `supernaturalDebt`.
- Use `openChoiceModal()` for rituals, readings, bargains, initiations, and consequences.
- Add a dedicated render function and call it from the central `render()` function.
- Add save/load normalization for every new occult collection and numeric field.

Potential thematic conflict: the current `spiritual` trait is framed as a benign stress-reduction characteristic. A darker occult system should avoid silently redefining that trait unless the design explicitly intends to do so.

---

## Shared integration infrastructure

### Modal system

The safest interaction path for all new systems is the existing modal infrastructure:

- `#modal`
- `#modalTitle`
- `#modalText`
- `.modal-actions`
- `#modalCancel`
- `#modalOk`

Markup is in `index.html:40`.

Helpers:

- `openModal()`
- `openChoiceModal()`

These helpers rebuild modal actions, provide cancellation, protect against dead-state actions, and trigger rendering after choices.

### Reusable CSS

`style.css` provides reusable generic structures:

- `.system-panel`
- `.system-copy`
- `.button-row`
- `.platform-grid`
- `.platform-card`
- `.lifestyle-grid`
- `.systems-grid`
- `.filter-btn`
- `.panel`
- `.goal`
- `.career-grid`

Relevant styles are in `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css:2-6`.

Responsive behavior:

- At 900px, `.systems-grid` becomes two columns.
- At 620px, system grids become one column.
- Buttons become flexible-width controls.
- System panels reduce their minimum height.

These styles are sufficient for legal, homelessness, and occult panels without introducing new layout primitives.

---

## Main integration risks

1. **State consistency**  
   Every new system must be added to `initialState()`, save/load object validation, field normalization, and rendering.

2. **Missing DOM targets**  
   Existing render functions generally guard with `if (!element) return`, but new systems should follow the same pattern so older or alternate markup does not break the game.

3. **Compressed HTML**  
   Much of `index.html` is written on very long lines, making targeted markup edits and review more error-prone.

4. **Modal action lifecycle**  
   New actions should use `runAction()` and existing modal helpers rather than bypassing them, otherwise dead-state handling, cooldowns, rendering, or save behavior may become inconsistent.

5. **Legal and homelessness overlap**  
   Evictions, tenant disputes, shelters, custody, and court cases could easily duplicate or conflict with existing landlord, prison, and family logic. Separate state ownership should be defined before implementation.

6. **Pet cap enforcement**  
   The load path caps pets at 12, but the live purchase action should also enforce that limit.

7. **No dedicated styling exists**  
   Legal, homelessness, and occult systems currently have no named CSS classes. They can reuse generic classes, but system-specific visual identity would require new selectors.

## Objective
- Expand VIVA into a polished Portuguese, offline, single-player life-simulation SPA with interconnected lifestyle, health, identity, social, property, collection, family, and future-progression systems.

## Requirements
- Preserve `SAVE_KEY = 'viva-save-v2'`, `localStorage`, centralized `state`, `render()`, `commit()`, `runAction()`, and `addEvent()` architecture.
- Preserve existing mechanics, dead-life guards, cooldown rollback, event ordering, save validation, sanitization, responsive UI, Portuguese labels, and visible feedback.
- Keep annual progression through `#ageBtn`; store temporal metadata for future monthly, quarterly, or action-based modes.
- Add visible biological and psychological attributes plus hidden `karma`, `madness`, fertility, and combat systems incrementally.
- Keep changes uncommitted unless explicitly requested.
- Browser visual verification is optional because Chromium is unavailable.

## Decisions
- Extend the existing architecture rather than replacing it.
- Normalize new persistent state through `initialState()` and validate/clamp it in `loadState()`.
- Keep annual progression active while storing `temporal.mode`, `lastAdvance`, and `totalMonths`.
- Integrate biological wear, fatigue, hunger, hydration, mental health, fertility, maximum HP, combat effects, madness, karma, and energy synchronization into `advanceYear()`.
- Reuse existing renderers, dashboard controls, modal flows, and Portuguese UI patterns.
- Use calculated `attributes.combatStrength` for annual conflict checks and fertility gating for family planning.
- Clamp persisted `attributes.maxHp` to the valid range `35–100`.

## Work State

### Completed
- Added normalized `temporal` state with annual mode, last advance year, and total elapsed months.
- Added normalized `attributes` state for intelligence, appearance, energy, mental health, fatigue, madness, fertility, aging, hunger, hydration, maximum HP, and combat strength.
- Added legacy-save merging, validation, sanitization, and clamping for temporal and biological attributes.
- Updated `advanceYear()` with temporal progression, aging, fatigue, hunger, hydration, mental-health, madness, fertility, max-HP, combat-strength, energy, health-cap, biological-wear, stress, and karma effects.
- Synchronized `attributes.energy` with `state.energy`.
- Updated combat display and annual conflict checks to use calculated `attributes.combatStrength`.
- Added fertility requirements and feedback to biological family planning.
- Added `renderAttributes()` and wired it into `render()`.
- Added Portuguese dashboard markup for temporal status and visible biological attributes.
- Added responsive styling for `.attributes-panel` and `.attributes-grid`.
- Updated temporal feedback with mode, next year, elapsed months, and aging wear.
- Preserved existing lifestyle, collections, exotic pets, landlord, addiction, mental health, identity, prison, finances, social media, family, and annual event systems.
- Updated `README.md` with VIVA documentation, execution, systems, persistence, and development checks.

### Active

### Blocked

## Next Move
1. If further work is requested, inspect the current VIVA files and make only targeted changes.
2. Re-run `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` after any edits.
3. Keep changes uncommitted unless explicitly requested.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: central state, save validation, rendering, actions, annual progression, attributes, combat, and family planning.
- `index.html`: Portuguese dashboard markup, annual progression control, temporal status, biological attributes, and family controls.
- `style.css`: responsive layout and styling, including `.attributes-panel` and `.attributes-grid`.

## Important Context

```

### Loading and validation

`loadState()` is implemented at `app.js:55-126`.

Its process is:

1. Read JSON from `localStorage`.
2. Merge it with a fresh `initialState()`.
3. Validate arrays such as:
   - `relationships`

7. Sanitize strings and collection sizes.

## 2. Rendering architecture

The main render entry point is `app.js:247-268`.

```js
function render() {
  const setText = (selector, text) => {
    const el = $(selector);
    if (el) el.textContent = text;
  };

  setText('#sideName', state.name);
  setText('#sideAge', `${state.age} anos · ${state.city}, ${state.country}`);
  setText('#money', money(state.money));

  // Top-level page and status updates omitted here

  renderEvents();
  renderPeople();
  renderFamily();
  renderCareer();
  renderEducation();
  renderAssets();
  renderHealth();
  renderNeeds();
  renderAttributes();
  renderHobbies();
  renderMentalHealth();
  renderPrison();
  renderFame();
  renderLifestyle();

  saveState();
}
```

Rendering is therefore both:

1. A UI update pass.
2. A persistence pass.

Most successful interactions eventually call `render()`, which means state changes are immediately reflected in the DOM and saved to `localStorage`.

### Specialized renderers

Important renderers include:

- `renderEvents()` — `app.js:132-133`

- `renderEducation()` — beginning at `app.js:301`
- additional career, relationship, family, health, and asset renderers later in the file

### Attribute rendering

`renderAttributes()` updates the attribute panel:

```js
function renderAttributes() {
  const a = state.attributes || {};

  const set = (id, value) => {
    const el = $(`#${id}`);
    if (el) el.textContent = `${Math.round(safePercent(value))}/100`;
  };

  set('intelligenceScore', a.intelligence);
  set('appearanceScore', a.appearance);
  set('mentalHealthScore', a.mentalHealth);
  set('fertilityScore', a.fertility);
  set('hydrationScore', a.hydration);
  set('hungerScore', 100 - a.hunger);
  set('fatigueScore', a.fatigue);
  set('maxHpScore', a.maxHp);

  a.energy = clamp(state.energy);

  const modes = {
    annual: 'anual',
    quarterly: 'trimestral',
    monthly: 'mensal',
    action: 'por ação'
  };

  const status = $('#temporalStatus');
  if (status) {
    status.textContent =
      `Modo ${modes[state.temporal?.mode] || 'anual'} · ` +
      `próximo avanço: ${state.year + 1} · ` +
      `${state.temporal?.totalMonths || 0} meses vividos`;
  }

  const note = $('#agingNote');
  if (note) {
    note.textContent =
      `${a.aging < 20
        ? 'Seu corpo ainda tem boa margem de recuperação.'
        : a.aging < 55
          ? 'O desgaste biológico pede hábitos consistentes.'
          : 'O envelhecimento está acelerado; cuide da saúde e do descanso.'} ` +

## 3. Action and dispatch flow

### Shared resource helpers

The core resource checks are at `app.js:134-160`:

- `setStat()`
- `changeStat()`
- `requireFunds()`
- `requireResources()`
- `requireEnergy()`
- `requireAge()`
- `canAct()`

Example:

```js
function requireResources(cost = 0, energy = 0) {
  cost = Math.max(0, safeNumber(cost));
  energy = Math.max(0, safeNumber(energy));

  if (state.money < cost) {
    toast(`Você precisa de ${money(cost - state.money)} a mais.`);
    return false;
  }

  if (state.energy < energy) {
    toast('Você está sem energia para isso. Descanse ou avance um ano.');
    return false;
  }

  state.money -= cost;
  state.energy = clamp(state.energy - energy);
  return true;
}
```

### Cooldowns

`runAction()` is defined at `app.js:162-169`:

```js
function runAction(key, action) {
  const previous = state.cooldowns[key];
  const newestEventBefore = state.events[0];

  if (!canAct(key, 1)) return;

  action();

  if (state.events[0] === newestEventBefore) {
    if (previous === undefined) {
      delete state.cooldowns[key];
    } else {
      state.cooldowns[key] = previous;
    }
  }
}
```

This means:

- An action first receives a cooldown.
- If the action successfully creates an event, the cooldown remains.
- If the action fails because of age, funds, energy, or another validation check, the cooldown is restored or removed.

### Commit flow

```js
function commit(message) {
  render();
  if (message) toast(message);
}
```

`commit()` is used by yearly progression. Other action paths often call `render()` directly from event handlers.

Some actions intentionally render more than once:

- `needsAction()` calls `runAction()` and then `render()`.
- `hobbyAction()` calls `runAction()`, then `render()`, and displays a success toast if a new event was added.
- Modal callbacks execute the action and then call `render()`.

---

## 4. Modal dispatch

Modal helpers are at `app.js:170-197`.

### Standard confirmation modal

```js
function openModal(title, text, action, confirm = 'Escolher este caminho') {
  const actions = $('.modal-actions');

  if (actions) {
    actions.innerHTML =
      '<button class="secondary-btn" id="modalCancel">Agora não</button>' +
      '<button class="primary-btn" id="modalOk"></button>';
  }

  $('#modalTitle').textContent = title;
  $('#modalText').textContent = text;
  $('#modalOk').textContent = confirm;

  $('#modal').classList.remove('hidden');
  $('#modalCancel').onclick = closeModal;

  $('#modalOk').onclick = () => {
    $('#modal').classList.add('hidden');

    if (state.dead) {
      toast('Esta vida chegou ao fim. Comece uma nova história.');
      return;
    }

    if (action) action();
    render();
  };
}
```

`openChoiceModal()` dynamically creates one button per choice. Each choice includes:

The selected action is executed only if the life is not dead, and the UI is then rendered.

`advanceYear()` begins at `app.js:481`.

The initial progression is:

```js

  return toast('Esta vida chegou ao fim. Comece uma nova história.');
}

state.age++;
state.year++;
state.temporal.totalMonths += 12;
state.temporal.lastAdvance = state.year;
```

### Attribute and biological changes

The yearly simulation updates:

- aging
- fatigue
- hunger
- hydration
- mental health
- madness
- fertility
- maximum HP
- combat strength
- energy

Examples from `app.js:485-496`:

```js
a.aging = clamp(
  (state.age - 24) * 1.15 +
  (state.age > 45 ? (state.age - 45) * .8 : 0)
);

a.fatigue = clamp(
  a.fatigue +
  7 +
  (state.stress > 65 ? 5 : 0) -
  (state.needs.sleep > 70 ? 8 : 0)
);

a.hunger = clamp(
  a.hunger +
  6 -
  (state.needs.nutrition > 65 ? 9 : 0)
);

  a.hydration -
  5 +
  (state.needs.nutrition > 60 ? 3 : 0)
);

a.mentalHealth = clamp(
  a.mentalHealth -
  (state.stress > 65 ? 5 : 1) -
  (a.fatigue > 70 ? 3 : 0) +
  (state.mental.treated ? 6 : 0)
);

a.fertility = clamp(
  a.fertility -
  (state.age > 35 ? 2 : 0) -
  (state.age > 50 ? 3 : 0)
);

a.maxHp = Math.max(35, Math.round(100 - a.aging * .35));
```

### Financial processing

The yearly simulation calculates:

- annual career income
- diet expenses
- exotic pet maintenance
- rental income
- annual expenses
- collectible value changes
- investment returns
- debt
- credit rating

Relevant section: `app.js:499-522`.

Income is not paid when the character is serving a prison sentence:

```js
const income =
  c.employed &&
  state.prisonYears === 0 &&
  !wasInPrison
    ? c.salary * 12
    : 0;
```

### Landlord system

Each year:

- eviction locks decrease
- completed evictions remove tenants
- overdue tenants lose credit
- tenants may become overdue
- vandalism may occur
- eligible rent is collected automatically

Relevant lines: `app.js:508-515`.

### Exotic pets

Pets can cause annual accidents:

```js
const petAccident =
  state.exoticPets.pets.length &&
  Math.random() < Math.min(.45, state.exoticPets.pets.length * .12);
```

An accident:

- increments `state.exoticPets.accidents`
- reduces health
- creates a warning event
- costs money

Relevant lines: `app.js:516-520`.

### Mental health and addiction

The yearly progression:

- increases or reduces addiction risk
- adds diagnoses for high stress or low happiness
- applies treatment benefits
- resets recovery status after sustained improvement

Relevant lines: `app.js:530-540`.

### Fame and social media

The simulation applies:

- annual follower growth
- engagement changes
- controversy decay
- fame growth
- brand income at sufficient fame

Relevant lines: `app.js:541-548`.

### Needs and relationships

Needs are adjusted yearly:

```js
state.needs.sleep =
  clamp(state.needs.sleep - 5 + (state.energy > 60 ? 4 : 0));

state.needs.social =
  clamp(state.needs.social - 3 + (state.relationships.length ? 2 : 0));

state.needs.nutrition =
  clamp(state.needs.nutrition - 2 + (state.money > expenses ? 3 : 0));

state.needs.purpose =
  clamp(state.needs.purpose + (c.employed ? 2 : -4));
```

Neglected needs increase stress and reduce health. Relationships lose affinity probabilistically, and children age by one year.

Relevant lines: `app.js:553-560`.

### Career progression

Employed characters receive:

- skill increases
- satisfaction changes
- possible promotions
- salary increases

Relevant lines: `app.js:561-565`.

### Events and history

Each year:

1. A yearly event is selected.
2. The event is added to the timeline.
3. Prison-related events may be added.
4. A history record is appended.

```js
state.history.push({
  year: state.year,
  age: state.age,
  money: Math.round(state.money),
  career: c.title
});
```

Relevant lines: `app.js:567-569`.

### Death conditions

The character dies if any of these occur:

- health reaches zero
- age reaches 105
- late-life random risk succeeds after age 92

```js
const reachedLimit = state.age >= 105;
const healthFailure = state.health <= 0;
const lateLifeRisk = state.age >= 92 && Math.random() < .15;

if (healthFailure || lateLifeRisk || reachedLimit) {
  state.dead = true;
  state.deathCause = healthFailure
    ? 'complicações de saúde'
    : reachedLimit
      ? 'idade avançada'
      : 'fim natural da jornada';

  addEvent(
    '☾',
    'O fim de uma jornada',
    `Sua história terminou por ${state.deathCause}, mas seu legado permanece.`,
    'pink'
  );
}
```

Finally, the year is committed and saved:

```js
commit(
  `Ano ${state.year}: ${
    income >= expenses
      ? 'suas contas fecharam no azul'
      : 'suas despesas exigiram atenção'
  }`
);
```

## 8. New-life creation and generations

`createLife()` is at `app.js:716-724`.

The previous life is archived:

```js
const archive = {
  name: previous.name,
  age: previous.age,
  year: previous.year,
  city: previous.city,
  country: previous.country,
  career: previous.career.title,
  money: Math.round(previous.money),
  cause: previous.dead
    ? (previous.deathCause || 'fim da vida')
    : 'nova jornada'
};
```

Inheritance is only granted after death:

```js
const liquidLegacy =
  Math.max(
    0,
    safeNumber(previous.money) +
    safeNumber(previous.finances?.investments) -
    safeNumber(previous.finances?.debt)
  );

const inheritance = previous.dead
  ? Math.round(liquidLegacy * .15)
  : 0;
```

The new life:

- starts at age `0`
- starts in year `2026`
- receives inheritance only if the prior life was dead
- has reset relationships
- starts with no active career
- retains up to 12 archived generations
- applies customizer values
- gives the selected talent a skill bonus
- creates a birth event
- hides the customizer
- renders and saves

Core reset:

```js
state = {
  ...fresh,
  name,
  city,
  pronouns: value('#newPronouns') || fresh.pronouns,
  country: value('#newCountry') || fresh.country,
  talent: value('#newTalent') || fresh.talent,
  trait: value('#newTrait') || fresh.trait,
  age: 0,
  year: 2026,
  money: inheritance,
  happiness: 75,
  health: 85,
  reputation: 10,
  stress: 25,
  generations: [...(previous.generations || []), archive].slice(-12),
  career: {
    title: 'Sem profissão',
    company: '—',
    salary: 0,
    level: 0,
    skill: 20,
    employed: false
  },
  relationships: []
};
```

- Preserve `SAVE_KEY = 'viva-save-v2'`, `localStorage`, centralized `state`, `initialState()`, `render()`, `commit()`, `runAction()`, and `addEvent()` architecture.

- Keep annual progression through `#ageBtn`, while storing temporal metadata for future monthly, quarterly, or action-based modes.
- Add visible biological and psychological attributes plus hidden `karma`, `madness`, fertility, and combat systems incrementally.
- Implement legal/family mechanics including alimony, child custody, criminal appeals, extradition challenges, and inheritance debt execution.
- Implement pet genetics and breeding with pedigree, purity, aesthetic mutations, sales, and behavior training.
- Implement employment and union mechanics including strikes, pickets, dismissal risk, and surprise drug tests based on hidden substance history.
- Implement homelessness and urban survival including begging, dumpster diving, squatting, cold/energy recovery, and police eviction risk.
- Implement occult systems including mediums, exorcists, haunted-property effects, karma-based rituals, alternative medicine, and poisoning risk.
- Keep changes uncommitted unless explicitly requested.

- Extend the existing architecture rather than replacing it.
- Normalize new persistent state through `initialState()` and validate/clamp it in `loadState()`.

1: # VIVA — simulador de vida
2: 
3: VIVA é uma SPA single-player em português sobre escolhas, consequências e novas gerações. A experiência funciona localmente no navegador, sem backend ou multiplayer.
4: 
5: ## Como executar
6: 
7: Abra `index.html` no navegador ou use o wrapper existente:
8: 
9: ```bash
10: ./start.sh
11: ```
12: 
13: O jogo também pode ser servido por qualquer servidor estático. `capture.sh` é um utilitário opcional para validação/capturas locais.
14: 
15: ## Sistemas
16: 
17: - avanço anual com renda, despesas, investimentos, dívidas, crédito, saúde, energia e envelhecimento;
18: - educação, habilidades, carreira, promoções, reputação e fama;
19: - relações com menus contextuais: escuta, programas, conversas difíceis, reconciliação, romance e planos de futuro;
20: - família, filhos biológicos ou adotivos, momentos exclusivos, apoio a interesses e conversas sobre sentimentos;
21: - histórico de eventos com resultados textuais, evolução de afinidade, papéis e impactos em felicidade, estresse, reputação e recursos;
22: - painel de legado entre gerações;
23: - patrimônio, metas financeiras, viagens e saúde;
24: - atividades com requisitos de idade, energia, dinheiro e cooldown anual;
25: - crime com risco de prisão, pena, multas e consequências persistentes;
26: - morte, herança parcial e arquivo de até 12 gerações;
27: - criação de novas vidas com país, cidade, personalidade, talento e aparência.
28: 
29: ## Persistência
30: 
31: O estado é salvo automaticamente no `localStorage` usando a chave `viva-save-v2`. Saves anteriores são mesclados com os valores padrão para manter compatibilidade quando novos sistemas são adicionados. Para recomeçar completamente, remova essa chave pelas ferramentas de armazenamento do navegador.
32: 
33: ## Desenvolvimento
34: 
35: A interface está dividida em `index.html`, `style.css` e `app.js`. O estado centralizado é atualizado por ações e sincronizado pela função `render()`. Para verificar a sintaxe do JavaScript:
36: 
37: ```bash
38: node --check app.js
39: ```

## File inspected

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js` — 726 lines

## Overall architecture

This is a single-file browser life-simulation application. It contains:

1. Utility functions and persistence.
2. A comprehensive mutable `state` object.
3. State normalization/loading from `localStorage`.
4. DOM rendering for each dashboard section.
5. Modal and action orchestration.
6. Gameplay systems: relationships, family, education, employment, mental health, prison, social media, lifestyle, collectibles, pets, landlord/property, finances, and aging.
7. Event-handler registration.
8. Initial `setupBindings(); render();`.

The save key is `viva-save-v2` at `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:1`.

---

## Utilities and persistence

### Utility functions — lines 2–17

- `$` / `$$`: DOM query helpers.
- `clamp`: constrains values to `0–100` by default.
- `money`: formats values as Brazilian currency.
- `pick`: random array selection.
- `today`: localized current date.
- `safeNumber`, `safePercent`, `safeColor`: basic value sanitization.
- `escapeHTML`: protects rendered user/state values from HTML injection.
- `mergeState`: recursively merges saved state into a fresh default state, preserving nested defaults where possible.

### Initial state — lines 19–53

`initialState()` returns the full default game state.

#### Scalar identity and life stats

```

#### Temporal state

```js
temporal: {
  mode: 'annual',
  lastAdvance: 2025,
  totalMonths: 0
}
```

Supported modes are annual, quarterly, monthly, and action, although the current age-advance binding uses `advanceYear()` directly.

#### Biological attributes

---

## Loading and normalization

### `loadState()` — lines 55–125

State is initialized with:

```js
let state = loadState();
```

`loadState()`:

1. Reads `localStorage.getItem('viva-save-v2')`.
2. Parses the JSON.
3. Merges it into `initialState()`.
4. Falls back to a fresh initial state if parsing fails.

### Array validation

The following properties are guaranteed to be arrays:

- `relationships`
- `events`
- `children`
- `generations`
- `healthConditions`
- `educationHistory`

Object-like arrays are filtered to remove nulls, primitives, and nested arrays.

### Nested object validation

The following sections are replaced with defaults if malformed:

- `career`
- `finances`
- `goals`
- `skills`
- `cooldowns`
- `needs`
- `hobbies`
- `mental`
- `addictions`
- `identity`
- `prison`
- `socialMedia`
- `lifestyle`
- `collectibles`
- `exoticPets`
- `landlord`
- `temporal`
- `attributes`

### Numeric and enum normalization

The loader:

- Clamps needs to `0–100`.
- Restricts temporal mode to:
  - `annual`
  - `quarterly`
  - `monthly`
  - `action`
- Ensures `lastAdvance` is at least 1900.
- Ensures `totalMonths` is nonnegative.
- Clamps most attributes to `0–100`.
- Restricts `maxHp` to `35–100`.
- Sanitizes addiction values.
- Ensures diagnoses are strings, max 8 entries, max 60 characters each.
- Sanitizes identity field types and limits `chosenName` to 80 characters.
- Restricts diet to:
  - `fastfood`
  - `balanceada`
  - `vegana`
  - `keto`
- Normalizes training values.
- Limits collectibles to 80 items.
- Limits exotic pets and landlord records to 12/20 entries.
- Sanitizes name, city, and country.
- Ensures age, year, and money are nonnegative or valid minimums.
- Clamps health, happiness, energy, and stress.
- Converts `dead` to a strict boolean.

Potential continuation note: several scalar fields such as `reputation`, `karma`, `fame`, `credit`, and parts of `career`/`finances` are not comprehensively normalized in `loadState()`, so new systems should continue using `safeNumber()`/`clamp()` when consuming them.

### Saving

`saveState()` — lines 127–130:

- Serializes the entire state back to `localStorage`.
- Updates `.save-state .dot` to green if present.

`render()` also calls `saveState()`, so most UI-driven state changes persist after rendering.

## Core action helpers

### Event and stat helpers — lines 131–160

- `toast(message)`: displays temporary feedback.
- `addEvent(icon, title, text, cls)`: prepends an event and caps the event list at 9.
- `setStat` / `changeStat`: mutate top-level percentage stats.
- `requireFunds`: validates and deducts money.
- `requireResources`: validates money and energy, then deducts both.
- `requireEnergy`: validates and deducts energy.
- `requireAge`: validates minimum age.
- `canAct`: implements year-based cooldowns.

### `runAction()` — lines 162–169

`runAction(key, action)`:

1. Saves the existing cooldown and newest event.
2. Calls `canAct`.
3. Executes the action.
4. If no new event was generated, restores the old cooldown.

This is the main mechanism preventing repeated actions in the same year. Actions that fail validation generally do not consume their cooldown because they do not add an event.

### `commit()` — line 161

Calls `render()` and optionally displays a toast.

---

## Modal system

### `openModal()` — lines 170–180

Creates a two-button modal:

- Cancel: `Agora não`
- Confirm: supplied label

The confirm callback:

1. Hides the modal.
2. Rejects actions if `state.dead`.
3. Executes the supplied action.
4. Calls `render()`.

### `openChoiceModal()` — lines 181–196

Creates a modal with:

- An intro text.
- A cancel button.
- One dynamically generated button per choice.
- Each choice has a label, optional detail tooltip, and action.

Choice actions also have dead-state protection and call `render()` afterward.

### `closeModal()` — lines 197

Hides `#modal`.

### Modal insertion point

New modal-driven systems should generally be added by:

1. Creating a menu function near the other menu functions, such as `educationMenu`, `relationshipMenu`, or `careerMenu`.
2. Calling `openModal()` for one confirmation action or `openChoiceModal()` for multiple branches.
3. Binding the entry point in `setupBindings()`.

---

## Rendering system

### Main `render()` — lines 247–268

Updates:

- Sidebar name, age, city, country, and money.
- Greeting and date/year.
- Happiness and reputation.
- Health card and progress bars.
- Mood description.
- Avatar.
- Relationship count.
- Net worth.
- Finance cards.
- Debt.
- Life/death status.

Then calls:

```js
renderEvents();
renderPeople();
renderFamily();
renderCareer();
renderEducation();
renderAssets();
renderHealth();
renderNeeds();
renderAttributes();
renderHobbies();
renderMentalHealth();
renderPrison();
renderFame();
renderLifestyle();
saveState();
```

### Supporting renderers

- `renderEvents()` — lines 133, called from `render()`
- `renderMentalHealth()` — lines 199–206
- `renderPrison()` — lines 207–210
- `renderFame()` — lines 212–220
- `renderLifestyle()` — lines 221–246
- `renderAttributes()` — lines 270–279
- `renderNeeds()` — lines 280–289
- `renderHobbies()` — lines 290–300
- `renderEducation()` — lines 301–312
- `renderAssets()` — lines 344–349
- `renderFamily()` — lines 350–360
- `renderCareer()` — lines 362–368
- `renderPeople()` — lines 370–378
- `renderHealth()` — lines 379–386

### Existing display insertion points

For new state-backed UI, the natural locations are:

- Add a renderer near the other `render*` functions.
- Invoke it from `render()` around line 268.
- Add event bindings in `setupBindings()` around lines 676–707.
- Ensure all generated HTML uses `escapeHTML()` for state-derived strings.

---

## Family and children

### Family rendering — lines 350–360

`renderFamily()` displays:

- Number of children.
- Each child’s name, age, and adopted/biological status.
- A `Cuidar` button for each child.
- Generational legacy records.
- Generation count.

Child buttons call `childMenu()`.

### Child interaction menu — lines 419–425

`childMenu(child)` offers:

1. **Tempo exclusivo**
   - Costs 6 energy.
   - Increases happiness.
   - Reduces stress.

2. **Apoiar um interesse**
   - Costs R$180 and 4 energy.
   - Increases happiness.
   - Adds an event.

3. **Conversar sobre sentimentos**
   - Costs 3 energy.
   - Increases happiness.
   - Reduces stress.

All actions use `runAction()` with child-specific cooldown keys.

### Biological child binding — lines 691–694

`#childBtn` opens a confirmation modal, then requires:

- Age 18 or older.
- An active `partnerId`.
- Fertility of at least 20.
- R$1,500.
- 12 energy.

A child is created with:

```js
{
  name,
  age: 0,
  adopted: false
}
```

### Adoption binding — lines 694–695

`#adoptBtn` requires:

- Age 21 or older.
- R$4,000.
- 16 energy.

An adopted child starts at age 2:

```js
{
  name,
  age: 2,
  adopted: true
}
```

### Annual child aging

`advanceYear()` increments every child’s age at line 560:

```js
state.children.forEach(child => {
  child.age = safeNumber(child.age) + 1;
});
```

---

## Pets

### State and display

Pets are stored in:

```js
state.exoticPets.pets
```

Each pet contains:

```js
{
  id,
  type,
  name,
  cost
}
```

`renderLifestyle()` displays pets at lines 227 and includes annual maintenance cost.

### Purchase — line 479

`buyExoticPet(type)` supports:

- `tigre`
  - Purchase cost: R$9,500
  - Annual maintenance: R$7,000

- `cobra`
  - Purchase cost: R$2,200
  - Annual maintenance: R$1,800

Requirements:

- Age 18 or older.
- Sufficient funds.

Purchasing increases stress and creates an event.

### Binding — line 689

Buttons with `[data-buy-pet]` call:

```js
buyExoticPet(button.dataset.buyPet);
render();
```

### Annual behavior — lines 501 and 516–520

- Annual pet maintenance is included in `expenses`.
- There is a random annual accident chance based on the number of pets.
- An accident:
  - Increments `state.exoticPets.accidents`.
  - Reduces health by 8.
  - Costs R$1,800.

---

## Landlord and property system

### State

```js
landlord: {
  properties: [],
  tenants: [],
  evictionLock: 0
}
```

Properties have:

```js
{
  id,
  name
}
```

Tenants have:

```js
{
  propertyId,
  name,
  rent,
  credit,
  overdue,
  vandalized,
  eviction
}
```

### Rendering — lines 228–245

`renderLifestyle()` renders:

- Property name.
- Tenant name.
- Rent.
- Credit score.
- Overdue status.
- Vandalism status.
- Eviction status.
- A legal-process notice when `evictionLock` is active.

### Actions — line 480

`landlordAction(type)` supports:

#### `property`

- Costs R$90,000.
- Creates a new property.
- Blocked while an eviction process is active.

#### `tenant`

- Finds the first property without a tenant.
- Assigns a random tenant.
- Generates rent between R$1,600 and R$2,500.
- Generates credit between 500 and 900.

#### `collect`

- Collects rent from tenants who are neither overdue nor being evicted.

#### `evict`

- Finds a tenant who is overdue or has vandalized the property.
- Sets `evictionLock = 2`.
- Marks the tenant for eviction.

### Binding — line 690

Buttons with `[data-landlord]` call `landlordAction()` and then render.

### Annual behavior — lines 502, 508–515

- Rent is included in annual income if the tenant is current and not being evicted.
- The eviction lock decreases annually.
- When the lock reaches zero, marked tenants are removed.
- Tenants can become overdue or vandalize the property randomly.
- Overdue tenants lose credit over time.
- Some overdue tenants can recover their status.

---

## Employment and career

### State

```js
career: {
  title,
  company,
  salary,
  level,
  skill,
  employed,
  satisfaction,
  remote
}
```

### Rendering — lines 362–368

`renderCareer()` displays:

- Employment status and level.
- Job title.
- Company and location.
- Satisfaction.
- Remote status.
- Salary.
- Skill bars.

### Career menu — lines 666–674

`careerMenu()` provides:

1. **Negotiate salary**
   - Costs 6 energy.
   - Usually raises salary by 12%.
   - Failure lowers satisfaction and raises stress.

2. **Develop a skill**
   - Costs R$180 and 10 energy.
   - Raises career skill, leadership, and satisfaction.

3. **Toggle remote work**
   - Costs 4 energy.
   - Changes satisfaction and stress.

4. **Resign / accept a new opportunity**
   - Resigning sets the career to unemployed.
   - Re-entering employment requires age 16 and 6 energy.
   - Completed education courses unlock specialized roles.
   - Without a specialized course, the player receives an analyst role based on education.

### Career binding — line 692

`#jobBtn` opens `careerMenu()`.

### Annual career progression — lines 499 and 561–565

During `advanceYear()`:

- Employed players receive annual salary income unless in prison.
- Career skill increases.
- Satisfaction changes based on remote status and stress.
- There is a 30% annual promotion chance while below level 10.
- Promotion increases level and salary by 8%.

---

## Relationships and partner system

### Rendering — lines 370–378

`renderPeople()` displays:

- Person name and role.
- Affinity.
- Romance status.
- Relationship progress.
- Interaction button.

### Relationship menu — lines 387–417

Actions include:

- Listen sincerely.
- Do an activity together.
- Speak honestly.
- Declare romantic feelings when romance is sufficiently high.
- Plan the future if the person is the current partner.

A partner is created by setting:

```js
state.partnerId = person.id;
```

The partner requirement is used by biological child creation.

### Annual relationship decay — line 559

Each relationship has a random chance of losing 2 affinity per year.

---

## `advanceYear()`

### Location

`advanceYear()` spans lines 481–579.

### Preconditions and time progression — lines 481–484

- Rejects advancement if the player is dead.
- Increments age and year.
- Adds 12 months to `temporal.totalMonths`.
- Updates `temporal.lastAdvance`.
- Reads the career object.

### Biological progression — lines 485–496

Updates:

- Aging.
- Fatigue.
- Hunger.
- Hydration.
- Mental health.
- Madness.
- Fertility.
- Maximum HP.
- Combat strength.
- Energy.
- Current health cap.

### Prison and employment income — lines 497–500

- Reduces prison time by one year.
- Suppresses salary during prison years and the transition year.
- Calculates annual salary income otherwise.

### Annual expenses and income — lines 500–507

Expenses include:

- Base living expenses multiplied by 12.
- Age-related expense inflation.
- Diet costs.
- Exotic pet maintenance.
- Training-related costs.

Income includes:

- Salary.
- Eligible landlord rent.

Investment returns are randomized between approximately -3% and +9%.

### Landlord processing — lines 508–515

Handles:

- Eviction countdown.
- Removal of evicted tenants.
- Tenant overdue status.
- Tenant credit changes.
- Vandalism.

### Pet accidents — lines 516–520

Randomly applies pet accidents, health loss, and money loss.

### Debt and credit — lines 518–522

- Negative annual balance becomes debt.
- Credit decreases by 35 when a deficit occurs.
- Otherwise debt is paid down slightly and credit rises by 8.

### Health, happiness, stress, and reputation — lines 523–529

Annual changes account for:

- Age penalty.
- Fatigue.
- Hydration.
- Hunger.
- Madness.
- Stress.
- Karma.
- Financial deficit.
- Personality trait.

### Addiction and mental health — lines 530–540

- Recovery reduces addiction levels.
- Active high-risk addictions increase stress and reduce health.
- Recovery ends after all addiction levels fall below 15.
- High stress can add an anxiety diagnosis.
- Low happiness can add a depression diagnosis.
- Treatment improves stress and happiness.
- Identity discovery slightly improves stress and happiness.

### Fame and social media — lines 541–548

- Followers grow or shrink based on controversy.
- Engagement changes annually.
- Controversy decays.
- Fame changes based on follower count and controversy.
- Fame of at least 60 plus employment creates annual brand income.

### Lifestyle and combat — lines 549–552

- Diet modifies health and energy.
- Combat strength can prevent a conflict.
- There is an annual robbery event, with combat training improving the outcome.

### Needs and relationships — lines 553–560

- Sleep, social, nutrition, and purpose decay or improve.
- Neglected needs damage health and increase stress.
- Relationships may lose affinity.
- Children age by one year.

### Career progression — lines 561–565

- Career skill and satisfaction update.
- Promotions may occur.
- Salary increases on promotion.

### Health conditions and yearly event — lines 566–569

- Players aged 45+ can develop high blood pressure.
- A random yearly event is added.
- Prison-related event text is added if applicable.
- A history snapshot is appended.

### Death conditions — lines 570–578

The player dies if:

- Age reaches 105.
- Health reaches 0.
- At age 92+, a random late-life death roll succeeds.

On death:

```js
state.dead = true;
state.deathCause = ...
```

A death event is added, then `commit()` renders and saves the state.

---

## Quick actions and activities

### `quickAction()` — lines 588–605

Supports:

- Education.
- Socializing with a selected relationship.
- Exploring:
  - Bookstore.
  - Trail.
  - Risky opportunity.
- Resting:
  - Sleeping.
  - Resting with someone.

### `needsAction()` — lines 607–616

Supports direct management of:

- Sleep.
- Social.
- Nutrition.
- Purpose.

### `hobbyAction()` — lines 617–652

Supports:

- Music.
- Fitness.
- Creativity.

Hobbies improve corresponding skills, needs, happiness, health, or stress.

### `activity()` — lines 653–665

Available activities include:

- Gym.
- Music.
- Volunteering.
- Casino.
- Dating.
- Meditation.
- Crime.
- Fame-seeking.

All activities use the modal system and generally route execution through `runAction()`.

### `modalAction()` — lines 708–714

Predefined modal actions:

- Study.
- Invest.
- Travel.
- Doctor/check-up.

---

## Event bindings

### `setupBindings()` — lines 676–707

Key bindings include:

- Navigation: `.nav-item`
- Quick actions: `.action-grid button`
- Activities: `.activity-grid button`
- Needs: `[data-need]`
- Hobbies: `[data-hobby]`
- Mental health: `[data-mental-action]`
- Prison: `[data-prison-action]`
- Social media: `[data-social-platform]`
- Celebrity actions: `[data-celebrity-action]`
- Diet: `[data-diet]`
- Training: `[data-training]`
- Collectibles: `[data-buy-collectible]`
- Pets: `[data-buy-pet]`
- Landlord: `[data-landlord]`
- Age advancement: `#ageBtn`
- Career: `#jobBtn`
- Dating: `#meetBtn`
- Biological child: `#childBtn`
- Adoption: `#adoptBtn`
- Quotes, settings, modal close, course selection, avatar, event ordering, property management, life creation, and appearance selection.

### Main insertion points for new systems

1. **State shape:** add fields inside `initialState()` around lines 19–53.
2. **Normalization:** add validation inside `loadState()` around lines 61–123.
3. **Rendering:** add a dedicated `renderX()` near lines 199–386, then invoke it from `render()` at line 268.
4. **Actions:** add standalone action/menu functions between existing systems, especially before `advanceYear()`.
5. **Annual progression:** add yearly logic inside `advanceYear()` lines 481–578.
6. **Bindings:** add selectors and handlers in `setupBindings()` lines 676–707.
7. **Modal actions:** add entries to `modalAction()` lines 708–714.
8. **Persistence:** no separate persistence hook is needed if the action calls `render()` or `commit()`, because `render()` calls `saveState()`.

```js

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand VIVA into a polished Portuguese, offline, single-player life-simulation SPA with interconnected lifestyle, health, identity, social, property, collection, family, legal, employment, survival, pet-breeding, and occult systems.

## Requirements
- Preserve `SAVE_KEY = 'viva-save-v2'`, `localStorage`, centralized `state`, `initialState()`, `render()`, `commit()`, `runAction()`, and `addEvent()` architecture.
- Preserve existing mechanics, dead-life guards, cooldown rollback, event ordering, save validation, sanitization, responsive UI, Portuguese labels, and visible feedback.
- Keep annual progression through `#ageBtn`, while storing temporal metadata for future monthly, quarterly, or action-based modes.
- Add visible biological and psychological attributes plus hidden `karma`, `madness`, fertility, and combat systems incrementally.
- Implement legal/family mechanics including alimony, child custody, criminal appeals, extradition challenges, and inheritance debt execution.
- Implement pet genetics and breeding with pedigree, purity, aesthetic mutations, sales, and behavior training.
- Implement employment and union mechanics including strikes, pickets, dismissal risk, and surprise drug tests based on hidden substance history.
- Implement homelessness and urban survival including begging, dumpster diving, squatting, cold/energy recovery, and police eviction risk.
- Implement occult systems including mediums, exorcists, haunted-property effects, karma-based rituals, alternative medicine, and poisoning risk.
- Keep changes uncommitted unless explicitly requested.

## Decisions
- Extend the existing architecture rather than replacing it.
- Normalize new persistent state through `initialState()` and validate/clamp it in `loadState()`.
- Keep annual progression active while storing `temporal.mode`, `lastAdvance`, and `totalMonths`.
- Integrate biological wear, fatigue, hunger, hydration, mental health, fertility, maximum HP, combat effects, madness, karma, and energy synchronization into `advanceYear()`.
- Use calculated `attributes.combatStrength` for annual conflict checks and fertility gating for family planning.
- Reuse existing renderers, dashboard controls, modal flows, and Portuguese action patterns.
- Add future systems through dedicated renderers, guarded action functions, annual progression hooks, and `setupBindings()` selectors.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added normalized temporal state with annual mode, last advance year, and total elapsed months.
- Added normalized biological attributes for intelligence, appearance, energy, mental health, fatigue, madness, fertility, aging, hunger, hydration, maximum HP, and combat strength.
- Added legacy-save merging, validation, sanitization, and clamping for temporal and biological attributes.
- Updated `advanceYear()` with temporal progression, aging, fatigue, hunger, hydration, mental health, madness, fertility, maximum health, combat strength, energy, health cap, biological wear, stress, and karma effects.
- Synchronized `attributes.energy` with `state.energy`.
- Updated combat display and annual conflict checks to use calculated `attributes.combatStrength`.
- Added fertility requirements and feedback to biological family planning.
- Added `renderAttributes()` and wired it into `render()`.
- Added Portuguese dashboard markup for temporal status and visible biological attributes.
- Added responsive styling for `.attributes-panel` and `.attributes-grid`.
- Updated temporal feedback with mode, next year, elapsed months, and aging wear.
- Preserved existing lifestyle, collections, exotic pets, landlord, addiction, mental health, identity, prison, finances, social media, family, and annual event systems.
- Updated `README.md` with VIVA documentation, execution, systems, persistence, and development checks.
- Verified `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` successfully.
- Inspected the complete current architecture, including state initialization/loading, renderers, action dispatch, family, pets, employment, property, modal, dashboard, and annual progression.

### Active
- Add normalized persistent state and validation for legal/family, pet breeding/genetics, employment/union, homelessness/urban survival, and occult systems.
- Implement guarded Portuguese actions, event feedback, annual effects, and modal flows for each pending subsystem.
- Add dashboard controls and renderers without disrupting existing systems.
- Update `README.md` after implementing the pending systems.

### Blocked
- Browser visual verification is unavailable because Chromium is not installed at `/home/runner/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1243/chrome-linux64/chrome`.

## Next Move
1. Add state defaults and `loadState()` normalization for the pending subsystems.
2. Implement legal/family actions and annual consequences, including alimony, custody, appeals, extradition, and inheritance debt.
3. Extend exotic pets with genetics, pedigrees, breeding, mutations, sales, and behavior training.
4. Add employment/union actions, substance-history drug-test risk, strikes, pickets, and dismissal consequences.
5. Add homelessness and urban-survival state, actions, annual cold/energy effects, and police eviction risk.
6. Add occult practitioners, rituals, haunted-property effects, alternative medicine, exorcism, karma interactions, and poisoning risk.
7. Add Portuguese dashboard markup, renderers, bindings, and visible feedback.
8. Update `README.md`, run `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`, and leave changes uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: central state, normalization, rendering, actions, annual progression, family, pets, employment, property, and modal systems.
- `index.html`: Portuguese dashboard sections, family controls, property/lifestyle controls, modals, and action entry points.
- `style.css`: responsive layout and panel styling, including biological attribute panels.
- `README.md`: current VIVA documentation and development checks.
- `.gitignore`: repository ignore configuration.
- `start.sh`: local application wrapper.
- `startup.sh`: auxiliary startup wrapper.
- `capture.sh`: optional browser visual-validation utility.

## Important Context
- Save key is exactly `viva-save-v2`; persistence is entirely through `localStorage`.
- Current `initialState()` includes `temporal`, `attributes`, `career`, `finances`, `collectibles`, `exoticPets`, `landlord`, family arrays, and existing addiction/identity/prison systems, but none of the newly requested legal, breeding, union, homelessness, or occult state.
- `loadState()` merges saves into `initialState()` and currently validates arrays plus nested objects such as `career`, `finances`, `lifestyle`, `exoticPets`, `landlord`, `temporal`, and `attributes`.
- `render()` calls existing renderers including `renderFamily()`, `renderCareer()`, `renderLifestyle()`, `renderAttributes()`, `renderMentalHealth()`, and `renderPrison()`, then saves state.
- `advanceYear()` increments age/year and `temporal.totalMonths`, processes income/expenses, landlord and pet effects, debt/credit, biological wear, addictions, relationships, children, career progression, events, and death.
- Existing pets are simple `{ id, type, name, cost }` records; existing employment only has career fields and career-menu actions.
- Existing family only models children and generations; existing legal-adjacent behavior is prison, arrest, landlord eviction, and basic partner/child/adoption flows.
- Existing action helpers are `requireFunds()`, `requireResources()`, `requireEnergy()`, `requireAge()`, `canAct()`, `commit()`, and `runAction()`.
- Changes remain modified and uncommitted.
